exposure: dyslipidaemia in the first trimester (defined by LDL-C > 3.24 mmol/L, TG > 1.92 mmol/L, HDL-C < 1.06 mmol/L, and TC > 5.39 mmol/L)
cohort: 36,256 pregnant women, with a specific focus on 952 patients diagnosed with subclinical hypothyroidism.
finding: Among pregnant women with subclinical hypothyroidism, elevated triglyceride dyslipidaemia was independently associated with gestational hypertension, and elevated LDL-C dyslipidaemia was associated with an increased risk of preeclampsia/eclampsia.
